examples.title: A small explanation
examples.note: Two independent responses to the same prompt. Differences alone do not establish a watermark effect or accepted output quality.

recording.prompt: In two sentences, explain how a seed becomes a tree to a curious adult.

ordinary.text: A seed starts as a tiny package with all the parts a growing plant needs, like food and instructions. When the seed gets the right mix of water, sunlight, and soil, it cracks open, and a new plant grows out of it, eventually becoming a tree.

marked.text: A seed starts as a tiny package with all the parts a growing plant needs. When the seed has the right conditions—like water, sunlight, and soil—it sprouts a small plant, which grows taller over time and becomes a tree.

examples.title: An everyday email
examples.note: Constraint failure: the marked response invents “the park around noon,” despite the prompt forbidding a time or location. Both responses add details. This run is retained for inspection, not approved as production-quality email.

recording.prompt: Write a warm, brief email inviting a friend to a picnic this weekend. Do not invent a date, time, location, or names. Use at most 60 words.

ordinary.text:
Hi [Name],  

Let’s grab some sunshine this weekend! Join me for a picnic — it’ll be fun, relaxing, and just us. Bring a blanket, snacks, and your smile. I’ll bring the rest. Let me know if you’re in!  

Can’t wait to catch up! 🌳🍴

marked.text:
Hi [Name],  

This weekend, let’s grab some lunch and enjoy the sunshine! Bring a blanket, snacks, and your good mood. We can meet at the park around noon. It’s been too long — let’s make it happen!  

Looking forward to it!  
[Your Name]

examples.title: Une idée en français
examples.note: Both samples stayed in French. This single pair does not establish multilingual quality or scientific accuracy.

recording.prompt: Explique en français pourquoi le ciel est bleu. Utilise deux phrases simples, sans traduire ta réponse en anglais.

ordinary.text: Le ciel est bleu parce que la lumière du Soleil est diffusée par les molécules de l'air. La lumière bleue, étant plus courte, est dispersée dans toutes les directions, ce qui donne au ciel son apparence bleue.

marked.text: Le ciel apparaît bleu car la lumière du Soleil, composée de différentes couleurs, est dispersée par les molécules de l'air. La lumière bleue, étant plus courte, est dispersée davantage que les autres couleurs, ce qui fait qu'elle domine dans le ciel.
